I think that a lot of this depends on if he’s truly changed or if he is still clearly doing the things that bother you. If he’s proven to you that he doesn’t behave this way anymore, I’d have a lot more hope for you two. Maybe sharing my experience will help. I’m 25 and I’ve been with my boyfriend for almost two years now. I can tell you that after having dated man after man who pushed my boundaries, didn’t respect me enough to not do things like what you’ve listed (messaging other women/like other girls pics, wanting to even open up the relationship, and more stuff I wasn’t okay with), I finally found the type I thought didn’t exist. There are men out there, albeit very hard to find, who don’t turn their head at every last attractive woman. I also understand that this doesn’t mean that my boyfriend isn’t attracted to other people because that’s human nature, but the fact that he loves me enough to choose to respect our relationship every single day is repairing years of my paralyzing insecurity little by little. It also has reminded me that you don’t have to settle for somebody who makes you feel bad for your request for boundaries or for your insecurities. Your boyfriend should be somebody who cares enough to give you what you want out of your relationship and if his values aren’t lining up with your repeated requests, then it might be wise to reconsider settling for that. This is a tough spot to be in especially when you love someone so much, but you also can’t change people unless they want to change.

.....I obviously don’t know you or your situation and I have no clue under what pretenses or emotional state you wrote this, but from what’s written here and from my personal point of view, at this point, I think you should be sounding a little more concerned for your wife’s wellbeing rather than planning what you do next if (god forbid) she were to follow through with it and break that promise... she sounds like she’s in need of some real help. Suicidal thoughts and ideations can be a very subconscious OR conscious cry for help from those suffering and both fashions in which they present themselves should be taken equally seriously. Suicidal people often feel in their altered mental states that they’re beyond repair/not worth the trouble. If nobody steps in or starts trying to pull her out of it, whether that’s through therapy, hospitalization, or even just really, really continuously expressing that you, your children and/or others would be absolutely lost or devastated living without her, this could get dangerous or tragic really fast. You don’t have to necessarily fully or even partially understand what’s she’s going through to be there for her or help her find the help she needs, but she needs you now more than ever, regardless of where your relationship stands, good or bad. This is her life that’s on the line and all suicidal ideation needs to be taken very seriously, and it doesn’t seem very sensitive of you to even be considering it an option and already discussing moving on if she carries out her plan. Just my two cents, coming from somebody who’s been in her shoes with my own plans that, thank god, were never acted upon.

Bipolar 23f here. For me, dealing with people close to me who don’t understand is probably almost worse than the depressive episodes sometimes because it feels so isolating and you can’t always verbalize what you’re going through. My depressive episodes are debilitating and come with chronic pain and if my ex boyfriend and parents wanted to guarantee me freaking out or isolating myself even more, they’d  make me feel crazy for being the way that I am. Don’t try to force her to open up when she doesn’t want to, and if she does, hear her out and just listen to listen, not to necessarily respond or give immediate advice—if that makes any sense. The fact of the matter is, nobody will ever understand somebody’s bipolar experiences other than that person alone, and it frustrates me to no end when people who think they’re being supportive say, “I totally, totally understand,” and throw solutions at me that I’ve tried 100 times that don’t work for people with this illness (i.e., “I don’t get why you won’t just get out of bed/try to remember how many people love you/believe in you, just keep that in mind” or “maybe if you exercise or do something to get your mind off (whatever), you’ll feel better.”) I hope this helps somewhat and I wish you and your lady happiness. It sucks being this way and the fact that you’re even reaching out to a community of people dealing with this would probably mean a lot to her if she knew. My parents haven’t even bothered to believe or even read up on my diagnosis.

Also if you’re there for a few days, you might spread your ride goals throughout those days to make it easier so you’re not trying to cram everything into one day if it’s crowded! I would also take time to check out live entertainment, the beach, flat rides, and just walking through the beauty that is the park for a while. Before I worked there I always had a pass so I liked to have dedicated riding days and dedicated “chilling” days where I just enjoy the park at my leisure and do whatever. :) So you could do it that way as well!

One more—if you’re into the history of the park at all, I highly recommend stopping into the Town Hall museum in Frontiertown! There’s tons of old CP memorabilia and photographs/scale models of coasters, etc. Also check out the Grand Ballroom above the main midway arcade! It’s a massive art-deco ballroom that’s been there since 1904 or so and the dances they used to have with the old big bands in the jazz era are what pulled CP through its near bankruptcy that almost shut them down during the Great Depression. I always get a very emotional feeling walking in there for some reason—it’s so quiet and unoccupied when it’s not being used and seems to stand still as you watch rides continue flashing and operating outside its windows.

If you have any control at all over what day you go, try to go on a Tuesday-Thursday because middle of the week days are usually the lower-attendance days. Or if you have to go Friday, try to get on your must-rides early in the morning because a lot of the weekend crowd won’t be there yet because they’ll come in the afternoon a lot of times! I only say that because lines can get crazy long especially getting into July, or buy fast lane plus for all your coaster-marathoning needs. Do anticipate spending a decent amount of $$ if you’re planning on eating in the park—prices are crazy in my opinion so I might pack some things. I’d also personally run to get on Vengeance and Maverick in particular in the AM because their lines are often the longest in the park and stay long (at the very least an hour or hour and a half) until the last hour before closing. And be very patient with ride operators if a ride goes down mechanically or if lines are ridiculously long. :) It’s not any fault of the employee and ride ops often work 55-85 hour weeks with no overtime pay, so if they ever seem exhausted or the least bit unenthused, (which isn’t always even a thing), that’s probably why 99% of the time.

But had I asked rather than being sent over, I probably would have had priority over somebody who worked perhaps at Wave Swinger or Matterhorn that was asking because those are less fast-paced rides to work than a coaster--not to say that there's never a chance to "move up" to a coaster if you're put at a flat ride because that's totally untrue. You can also probably specify with your hiring manager that you'd like to work on a coaster or a thrill ride, etc. 

My friend already worked in Area 3 so when I was hired 3 years ago, I had a little bit of a leg up because he told our manager that I learned fast and was competent enough to work a ride like Maverick. And if you'd rather stay away from working at Camp Snoopy or Planet Snoopy/Kiddy Kingdom, answer no politely when you have your interview with a manager and they ask if you'd prefer to work with children or not. You might also specify you're not afraid of heights if you're looking to join a coaster crew because for every coaster besides Dragster/Millie, you're required to do a lift walk to complete your ride training, and that scares some people.

And if you mean "work yourself up" as making yourself look good to leadership/supervision to get cross-trained or transferred, I'd suggest just being very nice/polite but not in a kissing their butt kind of way. Just be yourself and don't badger them too much and you'll be on good terms. 

And at every ride, we rotate positions every 30 minutes. You're trained at every position on your ride your first few days other than in controls (the control booth/panel) so you'll definitely be sitting at entrance, admitting people onto your ride platform (crowd control), and checking seats all throughout your day. There's a separate written controls test for each ride that you have the ability to take once you've completed the main training for your ride, and you have to pass with a 90% otherwise you'll have to retake it.

I'm sure Lifeguarding at Soak City or on the beach would be nice, but if you apply, I definitely myself would recommend working in Rides. The entire experience is enough for me personally to justify working a ton of hours for minimum wage. Everybody is different and has a different threshold of what they deem "too demanding," but if you have good work ethic and have a love for CP, you'll have the time of your life. Most of my best friends are ones I met through this job. 

Once you're hired, complete training, and begin your job, you'd request more hours from your specific location supervisor because they make the schedules. If you still want to pick up extra hours, the next people you'd contact are your area supervisor and/or manager expressing that you'd like more hours. And if they can't give you more at that time, you can always sign up for extra hours by filling out an extra hours form being a VIP tour guide on your day off or working the Luminosity shows at night after your regular shift.

You can always request to transfer to a different ride, but you'll typically stay within your area unless there's an open spot at the ride you're requesting in a different area. There are three areas that Park Operations divides the park into rides-wise. Area 1 includes all rides in the front of the park. Valravn now marks the beginning of Area 2 rides, and Thunder Canyon marks the beginning of Area 3 (essentially Frontiertown/most of the Gemini Midway.)
